justification: Standard: adds 10 data files and a download script (step 1 of ce-layers-own-copy-SCOPE-2026-11-18.md). Not Minor: the files will later feed the area check. Not Critical: nothing reads them yet, no database write, no behaviour change; the script never saves a partial copy.

pre_impl.existing_data: The area check asks 8 state map layers live per lot (services/lmr_area_inputs.LAYERS). spatial_overlays already holds bushfire, EPI heritage and coastal wetlands; it holds none of the 8 below. Live feature counts read 2026-11-18: TOD sites 9,597; accelerated TOD 8; exclusion 4; Hawkesbury-Nepean 11; Georges 1; coastal vulnerability 10; airport noise 29; State Heritage Register 1,825.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: I first assumed every layer would fit one file under the 2 MB repo limit; the State Heritage Register is 2.46 MB gzipped, so the script splits a big layer into numbered parts.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: New read-only downloader; scripts/ingest_spatial_overlays.py (the database loader) is unchanged and is used separately for the bushfire refresh.
pre_impl.external_source_error: The copy is as at the day it was read (read_on in the manifest). Coordinates are rounded to 6 decimal places (about 0.1 m). A changed live map is not seen until the script is re-run; step 3 of the plan adds the refresh and a comparison check.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: Nothing reads these files yet, so no answer changes. When step 2 reads them, a stale copy could say clear where the live map now says hit; the manifest date and the planned 45-day limit and comparison check are the answer to that.

falsifiable_check.fails_when: A saved file is edited or truncated, a layer or file is missing or stray, a file is over the limit, or the script writes a partial copy.
falsifiable_check.observed_red: Flipping one byte in lmr_exclusion.geojson.gz made 2 tests fail (hash and geometry checks); restored: 9 passed. Script tests: a failed page, a short layer and a failed layer in a batch each stop the copy or the manifest; a layer over the limit is split into parts.

functions.name: fetch_layer
functions.input: the web address of one state map layer
functions.output: every feature of the layer as GeoJSON in WGS84, or None
functions.if_none: a missing count, a failed page or a short layer returns None and nothing is saved

functions.name: round_coords
functions.input: nested lists of longitude and latitude numbers
functions.output: the same nesting with every number rounded to six decimal places

values: N/A - no value is read at runtime; the script copies map features once.
queries: N/A - no database query; the script reads public state map services over HTTP and writes files.

break_it.scenario: One page of a large layer cannot be read.
break_it.what_happens: A truncated map could be saved and later read as complete, clearing lots that are inside the layer.
break_it.how: fetch_layer returns None unless the feature count read equals the layer's own count; no file or manifest is written for a failed layer.

break_it.scenario: A saved map file is edited or corrupted later.
break_it.what_happens: The area check could read altered boundaries.
break_it.how: The manifest holds each file's sha256 and feature count and a test checks them; flipping one byte fails two tests.

break_it.scenario: A layer grows past the repo's 2 MB file limit.
break_it.what_happens: The commit would be blocked or the copy dropped.
break_it.how: The script splits it into numbered parts until each is under the limit and the test checks every file size.

post_merge.manual_verify: No - data files only; nothing reads them until step 2.
